name: Sida

project_scope.selection_mode: Two canonical learner species; compare without changing their separate unresolved native-range statuses.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Look for a small mallow flower with a staminal column, five calyx lobes, no epicalyx (involucel), and a dry segmented fruit (schizocarp). Then inspect whether the stem creeps or stands erect, the hairs on its nodes, and the mericarp tips.
shared_traits: Herbs or subshrubs with simple stipulate leaves, commonly bearing stellate hairs
Small axillary flowers with five petals and a staminal column, not a head of many florets
Mature dry schizocarp splitting into one-seeded mericarps; mericarp structure matters for identification
visual_learning_order: Confirm Sida by calyx without epicalyx and segmented dry fruit
Examine petiole-base tubercle, hair types and mature mericarp tips

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: Long, freely branching procumbent stems spreading along ground
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Usually erect or ascending herb/subshrub, ca. 0.2–1 m; not characteristically procumbent

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: No diagnostic spinelike tubercle reported in current canonical account; verify nodes rather than assuming absolute absence
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Small spinelike tubercle usually just below petiole attachment; may be absent, and is not a true spine

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: Usually 1–2 mm simple hairs mixed with multirayed stellate hairs (FNA key)
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Minute stellate hairs, generally to 0.5 mm (FNA)

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: Small ovate-oblong leaves; crenate margins extend toward base, leaves distributed along prostrate stems
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Ovate to lanceolate/narrow oblong, about 2–6 cm; margins crenate-serrate to base, often subcordate base

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: Small axillary flowers; do not identify by petal color; exact style branch count requires matched confirmation
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Solitary or 2–4 axillary flowers, calyx 5–7 mm; 5 style branches (FNA)

species_comparison_matrix.abutilifolia: Slightly rugose mericarps (FNA key); record count and apical spines from verified mature local material
species_comparison_matrix.spinosa: Schizocarp 4–5 mm across; 5 mericarps, each 3–4 mm, with apical spines ca. 1 mm (FNA)

field_comparison_steps: Photograph entire plant at soil line: trailing stems versus erect branches.
At several intact nodes photograph the stem immediately below each petiole; note a tubercle if present, but absence does not exclude S. spinosa.
Magnify stem hairs against a scale: mixed long simple + stellate versus uniformly minute stellate.
Confirm five-lobed calyx and central staminal column on an open flower.
Collect photographs (not necessarily specimens) of fully mature dry schizocarps from side and top with a millimeter scale; count mericarps and examine tips.
overlap_cautions: Both species have small, toothed leaves, axillary flowers, and stellate hairs; no single leaf photo is a safe determination.
S. spinosa's petiole-base tubercle is often present but sometimes absent; FNA explicitly notes that it is not a true spine.
Growth form can be affected by disturbance and mowing; verify nodes, hair and fruit characters.
Fruit characters require mature schizocarps; immature flower/fruit photos are insufficient for counts or apical-spine comparisons.
Both canonical species currently have UNRESOLVED target-zone native-range labels; learner inclusion is not certification of local nativity.
The spelling S. abutilifolia is retained as the current canonical ID; do not silently create a separate card for alternate spellings or historical synonyms.

local_lookalikes.separator: Compare larger flowers, style branch counts and the mature mericarp architecture rather than just fuzzy mallow leaves.
Examine calyx/epicalyx, leaf divisions and fruit segments; flowers may resemble Sida at a glance.

Also procumbent; FNA key contrasts apically crowded leaves and teeth restricted toward the leaf tip with evenly distributed, crenate-to-base leaves of S. abutilifolia. Do not imply local occurrence without evidence.
Furled petals and fleshy fruit instead of Sida's small open flower and dry mericarps.

handoffs.question: Verify exact mericarp count and apical spine architecture for S. abutilifolia from authoritative descriptions and matched mature local material; compare against the five, ca. 1 mm-spined mericarps of S. spinosa. Confirm whether tubercle absence in S. abutilifolia is a reliable key character.

look_here_first: First compare the whole-plant habit in the two actual species photographs: Sida abutilifolia spreads across the ground; Sida spinosa is usually upright. Then photograph intact nodes for S. spinosa's sometimes-present petiole-base tubercle, and ripe mericarps for confirmation. Don't identify these mallows on yellow flowers alone.

visual_lesson.title: Two fanpetals: follow the stem before the flower
visual_lesson.intro: Both photographs are locally installed, licensed whole-plant views. They help you compare growth habit, but they are not magnified proof of tubercles, hairs, staminal columns or fruit spines.
visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole-plant posture → node below petiole → close-up stem hairs → calyx and staminal column → ripe segmented fruit

steps.title: 1 · Spreading fanpetal
steps.look_for: Trace the main stems outward along the ground; leaves continue along the sprawling branches. Do not assume the tiny hairs are resolved at this scale.
steps.why_it_matters: Ground-hugging, freely branched habit is a useful starting cue for S. abutilifolia.

steps.title: 2 · Upright prickly sida
steps.look_for: Compare the generally erect or ascending main stems with the spreading species. The diagnostic small tubercle below the petiole is NOT proven by this whole-plant shot.
steps.why_it_matters: Habitat-disturbed stems can bend, but habitual growth direction narrows the pair quickly.

steps.title: 3 · The tubercle is at the NODE, not a branch thorn
steps.look_for: Check immediately below several petiole insertions for the small spinelike projection; it can be missing. It is not a true spine.
steps.why_it_matters: One of the most memorable S. spinosa clues, with an important absence caveat.

steps.title: 4 · Compare hairs, not fuzzy impressions
steps.photo_role: future side-lit matched stem hair macros
steps.look_for: S. abutilifolia may show longer 1–2 mm simple hairs mixed with stellate hairs; S. spinosa has much shorter stellate hairs. Photograph with a scale.
steps.why_it_matters: Hair type is much stronger than vague leaf fuzziness.

steps.title: 5 · Find the ripe mericarps
steps.photo_role: future matched dry schizocarp top and side views
steps.look_for: Document the mature segmented fruit, count its sections and inspect each tip. S. spinosa commonly has five spined mericarps; do not transfer that number to S. abutilifolia without confirmation.
steps.why_it_matters: The ripe fruit supplies botanical confirmation when habit overlaps.
